notes: Two models kept apart by "model": Javelin (1968-74; the 1971-74 AMX is a Javelin trim, shown in trims) and AMX (1968-70 two-seater; 1977 Hornet AMX, 1978 Concord-based AMX, 1979-80 Spirit AMX). NHRA = nhra_javelin-amx.json, never listed in sources. All AMC literature (brochures, AMX Story, 1980 Data Book) counts as ONE manufacturer source; all Wikipedia articles count as ONE; the two Hagerty articles count as one. confirmed = NHRA + 2 independent non-NHRA sources; three_sources_not_nhra = 3 independent non-NHRA sources. HP gross through 1971, SAE net from 1972. AMC 1968-74 engine charts were read from the brochure page images (OCR plus visual check). The Mark Donohue Javelin is a 1970 model, not 1971: 360/290 standard, 390/325 optional. Not recorded: 343 2-bbl (235 hp) and 232 2-bbl (155 hp) in the Javelin (Wikipedia/MuscleCarFacts list them, but AMC's 1968-70 charts give them only to Rebel/Ambassador/Hornet); the 1970 390/340 (Rebel Machine only); a special-order 1978 AMX 401 (Wikipedia only); the 1969 Mexico-only 252 and later Mexico-only 282 sixes. The EPA input is empty (all years are before 1984). Blocked or unusable: Hagerty valuation tool (redirect), allpar, Hemmings, Drivingline (factual errors). musclecarfacts.com refused connections late in the run; the 1969 AMX and some 1973-74 statements come from search excerpts and are marked as such. MuscleCarFacts year pages contain errors (e.g. 1971 360 4-bbl given as 290 hp, 1974 195-hp 360 labelled 2-bbl), so they are cited only where they agree with AMC.
